newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Clariant declines comment on Hoechst.
newsitem.headline: Clariant declines comment on Hoechst.

text.p: Swiss group Clariant AG declined to comment on an announcment by Germany's Hoechst AG that the two companies would merge their speciality chemicals businesses.
A Clariant spokesman queried by Reuters said the Swiss group expected to make a statement later in the day, probably after 2:00 p.m. (1300 GMT).
"We have no comment for the moment," a spokesman said.
Asked whether a statement would be coming, the spokesman said yes and added that it was more likely after 1300 GMT than before that time.
Hoechst earlier announced in Frankfurt that it would merge its specialty chemical business with Clariant and take a large minority stake in the Swiss company.
Clariant is one of the world's leading manufacturers of textile dyes and chemicals. It also produces dyes and chemicals for leather, paper and plastics.

Clariant was spun off as a specialty chemicals unit by Sandoz AG last year as part of Sandoz's concentration on pharmaceuticals and nutrition ahead of its planned merger with Ciba-Geigy AG as the new firm Novartis AG.
